title: Workspace teardown via cx.realm.tombstone cascade preserves audit trail

preconditions.comment: §10.1 specifies teardown uses standard cx.realm.tombstone events; there is no agent_workspace-specific teardown event kind. realm_id is an Event-envelope top-level field, not a payload field (event-payload.schema.json space_tombstone_payload is additionalProperties=false).

input_steps.design_note: Tombstone on workspace root Realm starts the cascade (§10.1 step 1). Per space_tombstone_payload, only reason / replacement_space / replacement_event / effective_at are allowed in payload.

Mirror Realms linked via derived_from(workspace_root); housekeeping cascades tombstone (§10.1 step 2). The derived_from linkage itself lives on the mirror Realm's profile / state, not inside this tombstone event payload.

expected_post_state_invariants: all mirror agent_task cells unreachable (§10.1 step 3)
execution_state cell no longer readable on tombstoned mirror Realm
source-Realm mention_redirect events PRESERVED (audit trail irreversible, §10.1 step 4)
authority_grant_ref in those mention_redirect events still resolves to source-Realm grants
DID Document ContrixAgentWorkspaceService entry removed (§10.1 step 5)

audit_trail_durability.mirror_space_content: unreachable but addressable by anchor index until compaction

design_note: Teardown is NOT atomic at the protocol surface — it is a cascade of standard cx.realm.tombstone events. The audit anchor is the tombstone anchor pinned by the workspace root tombstone; external systems can reference this anchor after Realms compact away.
